Diabetes insipidus and SIADH: 1

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

After pituitary surgery, a patient develops large volumes of dilute urine and rising sodium. Urine concentration improves with desmopressin during appropriate assessment. Which vasopressin-related disorder best explains the deficient hormone effect in this case?

  1. Osmotic diuresis
  2. Arginine vasopressin deficiency
  3. Arginine vasopressin resistance
  4. SIADH
  5. Free-water loss
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Arginine vasopressin deficiency

Central diabetes insipidus results from inadequate vasopressin secretion and can respond to desmopressin.

Understanding the options

Arginine vasopressin deficiency
Central diabetes insipidus results from inadequate vasopressin secretion and can respond to desmopressin.
Arginine vasopressin resistance
Nephrogenic diabetes insipidus reflects reduced renal response to vasopressin. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
SIADH
Hypotonic hyponatremia with inappropriately concentrated urine can suggest SIADH after excluding relevant alternatives. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
Free-water loss
Inadequate antidiuresis produces dilute polyuria and can cause hypernatremia if water intake does not keep pace. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
Osmotic diuresis
Glucosuria or another poorly reabsorbed solute can cause polyuria without primary vasopressin deficiency. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
